newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Global reaches buyout offer level.
newsitem.headline: Global reaches buyout offer level.

text.p: A five percent rise in shares in Hungarian retailer Global Rt to the buyout level of 2,100 forints was a completely normal phenomenon on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday, traders said.

Global shares rose more than 11 percent on Monday after Tesco, which holds more than 96 percent of Global via a Netherlands-based subsidiary, made a buyout offer to holders of Global shares at 2,100 forints or 7.48 pounds.
Global shares are planned to be delisted from the BSE.
"The company is buying the shares back at 2,100 forints, thus the rise to this level is quite normal," one trader said.
Global opened at 2,010 forints, above Monday's closing price of 2,000 forints, and rose continuously in slack trade.

The trader did not exclude the possibility, however, that the share might surpass 2,100 forints as there may be investors who wished to maintain their stakes in Global despite a Tesco stake of over 96 percent.
